lines.text: This snake doesn't just slither away from danger. It rolls, like a wheel.
These are dwarf reedsnakes: tiny, secretive snakes from Borneo.
Scientists in Japan filmed 13 of them, from three species, with cameras at different angles.
When they roll, they hit up to 3.7 metres per second. That's about four times faster than their top slithering speed.
But the body doesn't spin like a stiff tube. One side whips forward and strikes the ground, then the other side. Left, right, left, right.
The strangest part? While the body tumbles, the head stays steady, facing forward.
They can even roll along a track just 20 centimetres wide.
The study, from Toho University, is published in Current Biology. Sometimes the fastest escape is to stop slithering and start rolling.
